test_title: PYST 4: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is considered a poor file management practice on a computer system?

options.text: Giving files meaningful and descriptive names
Saving temporary files in unrelated and scattered folders
Creating separate folders for documents, images and videos
Using nested folders to organise large sets of data

solution:
The correct answer is __**Saving temporary files in unrelated and scattered folders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Saving temporary files in unrelated and scattered folders:**

 
 
• This is a poor file management practice as it leads to **disorganization**, making it difficult to locate files when needed. Scattered files across multiple folders result in wasted time searching for data.
 
• When temporary files are saved in unrelated folders, they can disrupt the intended folder structure and organization, creating a chaotic system.
 
• Unrelated and scattered storage increases the risk of **data duplication**, loss, or accidental deletion.
 
• It can also negatively affect the **performance of the computer system** due to cluttered storage and difficulty in performing system maintenance tasks.
